before_after.subtitle: One system, in production, with measured numbers. The client stays anonymous, the mechanism does not.
before_after.case_challenge: The same jewelry, sold in store and online. Every piece is one of a kind, so a double sale is not an inconvenience, it is a cancelled customer.
before_after.case_before_1: One person watched orders all day, to see whether the piece was in the warehouse or in a store.
before_after.case_before_2: For every store order they called the salesperson and read out the item code.
before_after.case_before_3: The salesperson left the customer in front of them, searched the display case, and called back.
before_after.case_before_4: If nobody caught the order in time, the piece had already left the store.
before_after.case_after_1: The order finds its own store, from the product code.
before_after.case_after_2: The whole store team gets the item, code and price on Telegram, with two buttons.
before_after.case_after_3: Whoever taps first takes the order, and the manager gets the confirmation automatically.
before_after.case_after_4: Product photos are prepared automatically, not one at a time.
before_after.case_note: The numbers come from the system's own execution logs and the client's operational data. Where an estimate was needed, we used the conservative one.

faq.title: FAQs
faq.subtitle: Common questions about operational transformation and what to expect.
faq.q1: How is this different from just using ChatGPT ourselves?
faq.a1: ChatGPT is a tool. What we build is a system. We connect AI to your data, workflows and existing software so work gets executed automatically instead of just answered in a chat window. The difference is the same as having a hammer versus having a factory.
faq.a2: We work with businesses that already work and want to scale without adding people at every step. The industry matters less. What matters is that operations have reached the point where growth brings more work, not more freedom.
faq.q3: What does the first month actually look like?
faq.a3: It starts with an operational assessment, 3 to 5 working days. You see your processes laid out, find out where time and money are lost, and get a report with concrete, prioritized steps, presented live. The fee is credited toward the next project if you start within 30 days. After the assessment you know exactly what gets built and in what order, and implementation runs incrementally, tested alongside your existing process.
faq.q4: What if the AI makes a mistake?
faq.a4: Every system includes human checkpoints for critical actions. AI handles volume, humans handle judgment. Performance is monitored continuously, and issues are caught before they become operational problems.
faq.q5: Do you work with businesses outside Romania?
faq.a5: Yes. Most client relationships are fully remote and async. We deliver the same way we would in person.
faq.q6: Do we need to change our existing software?
faq.a6: No. We plug into the tools you already use. If a platform exposes an API, we integrate directly. If it does not, we deploy automation agents that interact with the software the same way a human operator would.
faq.q7: What if we're not sure what should be automated first?
faq.a7: Most businesses already know where the friction is. Reporting delays, repetitive admin work, disconnected systems, slow handoffs between teams. We identify which processes create the biggest operational drag and prioritize based on ROI, implementation speed and complexity.
faq.q8: Will this disrupt our current operations?
faq.a8: No. Systems are deployed incrementally and tested alongside your existing workflows before going fully live. The goal is to improve operations without interrupting them.
faq.a9: We measure operational impact. Time saved, fewer manual tasks, reduced errors, faster reporting, quicker response times and better visibility across the business. The objective is not more AI. The objective is smoother operations.

calculator.title: What it costs you right now, per month
calculator.subtitle: Two questions about revenue, two about time. The maths runs in your browser, nothing is sent anywhere.
calculator.events_label: Enquiries or orders lost per month
calculator.events_hint: The ones nobody got to in time, or that fell through along the way
calculator.avg_label: What one is worth on average (RON)
calculator.hours_label: Hours of manual work per week
calculator.hours_hint: Copying between systems, checking, reporting done by hand
calculator.rate_label: What an hour of staff time costs you (RON)
calculator.disclaimer: This is an estimate from your own numbers, not a promise. The operational assessment replaces the estimate with figures taken from your real processes.
calculator.intro_1: A business gets stuck in two ways. Either not enough people want what you sell, or you cannot keep up with the ones who already do.
calculator.intro_2: If it is the first, you have a marketing problem, and this calculator will not help you at all. If it is the second, more promotion actually makes things worse: you pour more enquiries into a system that is already losing them.
calculator.intro_3: The second kind of stuck carries a cost almost no business ever sees, because it never lands on an invoice. It is not a cost, it is something that simply stops happening. It comes in two shapes: the enquiries nobody got to in time, and the hours your people spend moving data from one place to another instead of doing the work you hired them for.
calculator.intro_4: Both can be put into numbers. That is all the calculator below does: it shows you, with your own figures, what that adds up to in a month and in a year.
